task_instance: Add EAS Observe instrumentation to a minimal Expo SDK 57 app: install the real expo-observe npm package, wrap the root component with ObserveRoot, mark the app interactive with the useObserve() hook, and log a custom event via Observe.logEvent, then verify the integration typechecks against the actual published package types.
evidence: Scaffolded a blank-typescript Expo app (SDK 57) at sample-app/ via `npx create-expo-app@latest sample-app --template blank-typescript`. Installed the real published package with `npm install expo-observe@57.0.24` (npm view confirms it is a genuine Expo package, dist-tag sdk-57: 57.0.24). Inspected the package's shipped .d.ts files (node_modules/expo-observe/build/index.d.ts, ObserveRoot.d.ts, useObserve.d.ts, and expo-app-metrics/build/types.d.ts) to confirm the exact API surface the skill describes (ObserveRoot, useObserve().markInteractive, Observe.logEvent, ObserveErrorBoundary all present, matching SKILL.md's SDK 56+ guidance). Rewrote sample-app/App.tsx to wrap the root with <ObserveRoot>, call markInteractive() from useObserve() in a useEffect, and log a custom event with Observe.logEvent('button_pressed', { attributes: { screen: 'home' } }) (fixed one initial type error: LogEventOptions takes an `attributes` map, not arbitrary top-level keys). Verified the deliverable by running `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`, which completed with zero errors, i.e. the instrumented app compiles cleanly against the real expo-observe/expo-app-metrics type definitions. Also confirmed the CLI half of the skill is real and installable: `npx eas-cli observe:metrics-summary --help` printed the full flag list (--platform, --metric with nav_cold_ttr/nav_tti/etc., --stat, --json, ...), matching the skill's queries reference. Did not attempt to actually run `eas observe:*` against live data or an EAS project, since that requires an authenticated EAS account and a real production build reporting metrics (paid/account-bound service, explicitly out of scope per the sandbox's safety rules and the skill's own 'EAS service - costs apply' banner). The core deliverable exercised here -- correctly adding EAS Observe instrumentation to a project's code -- was fully produced and verified without needing any account, credentials, or paid service. Files produced: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec/expo__skills__eas-observe/sample-app/App.tsx and package.json.
